items.title: Route freely over pedestrian areas

labels.name: Routing
labels.description: Route building issues, e.g. valid route, valid ETA

items.body:
The routing algorithm should be able to route freely over pedestrian areas. Their minimal tags look like this:
```
area=yes
highway=pedestrian
```
Note that other access specifications also apply. For example, if there's an additional `bicycle=yes` tag then bicycles should be able to route over them as well.

Right now, the routing algorithm routes along the edges of a pedestrian area. I imagine routing freely over an area is quite different from how the routing algorithm was designed to work. However, maybe a way of doing it would be to make it possible to route from any node of the area to any other node, if there's a line of sight, so, don't allow a node -> node route if following that straight line would make you leave the area.

Note that it is also possible for areas to have 'holes', these are done using multipolygon relations. If a pedestrian area has a hole in the center, for example, because there's a fountain there, the routing algorithm should route around that as well.

I feel like this could be done with relatively little changes to the routing engine if you give it all possible paths between all nodes as ordinary paths, but that will probably significantly increase computation time and memory usage. Maybe it's a good idea to only do this for nodes along the edge if they are at least a distance of x apart, that way you reduce cost for areas that are severely over-noded and don't really lose out on route quality.

In the attached drawing, the gray polygon is the pedestrian area, the brown lines are paths. When routing from one path to the other, the red line is how it's currently done, the green line is how it could be done.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/29862810/209432453-c44eaef8-bbba-48b9-8ed0-48c0e6f32d19.png)

What do you think?

items.title: Pedestrian navigation improvements including compass rotations

labels.name: Navigation
labels.description: Issues related to the active Navigator / Navigation mode

items.body:
Perspective view is quite useless for pedestrian navigation due to low speeds and it makes harder to pan the map. I suggest turning it off by default for pedestrians or providing an easy way to turn it on/off, because going to the settings every time one gets into or off a car is cumbersome. Another (automatic) option is suggested in #2055.

The app is slow recalculating the route when a user diverts from it (and its a much more common situation for pedestrians compared to car nav) and is slow updating distance and time left when a user switches device on after keeping it off for a minute. To clarify - its not because of slow gps fix - usually there is a long pause between the fix and route update/recalculatuon.

There are a lot of small but annoying map rotations to the left and to the right. There is no such a thing in a car nav mode, because the direction is based on a stable speed vector I suppose. But in pedestrian mode the speed is low and my guess is the app uses a compass or a gyroscope which gives a lot of noise - some filtering is required.

items.title: Crossing-aware voice directions for walking and cycling navigation

labels.name: Enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request, an improvement of some existing feature

items.body:
In areas with highly mapped pedestrian and bicycle infrastructure basic "Turn right" voice directions, while still actionable, suffer from some ambiguity. While approaching a street with two parallel paths on both sides, distinguishing between "turn left onto the sidewalk", "turn left onto the street", and "turn left to the sidewalk on the other side of the street" may be difficult, especially at speed.

My suggested solution to this would be to make voice directions "crossing-aware", in that whenever a direction is either preceded or followed by a road crossing, it should be made clear in the spoken directions. Further distinguishing between streets and roads will help with keeping it clear which way a given crossing goes.


## Example scenarios

Direction, preceded by a crossing
1. `In x meters, cross the street, then turn right`
2. `Turn right`

![image](https://github.com/organicmaps/organicmaps/assets/4138317/16bd1bde-d24a-4d65-83e6-a8c177147e6b)


Direction, followed by a crossing, followed by a direction
1. `In x meters, turn right and cross the road, then turn left.`
4. `Turn right, and after crossing the road, turn left.`
5. `Turn left`

![image](https://github.com/organicmaps/organicmaps/assets/4138317/ca6fdd4b-9e97-4fd3-8b2d-848ae5c32e98)

"Keep right" direction, preceded by a crossing
1. `In x meters, cross the street, then keep right`
2. `Keep right`

![image](https://github.com/organicmaps/organicmaps/assets/4138317/fff8ef4a-61f3-4af0-a4df-ce172f32a348)

## Other considerations

Street for `residential` and other, road for `tertiary` and larger.

Road types that should be ignored at the very least include `driveway` and `service`. In general, crossings shouldn't need to be their own direction type, rather a feature that modifies a direction that is given (ie. no standalone "cross the road"). 

Where available, street names could also be used instead of `the street/the road`. This might push the announcements to be a bit too long though depending on road naming convention.

items.title: [iOS Feature] add HealthKit integration to add cycling / walking distances to Apple Health
items.body:
On iOS Apple Health allows to add cycling or walking distances to Apple Health. Many people use apps to add their cycling and running into Apple Health.

It would be awesome if it was possible to add cycling or walking distances to Apple Health directly from Organic Maps. Once HealthKit is supported, Organic Maps would show up in Health app > Sharing > Apps.  Selecting Organic Maps would then allow to enable individual activities like `Cycling Distance`or `Walking + Running Distance`. Whenever a user then uses Organic Maps to cover walking or cycling distance, that distance would be reflected in Health app with nice stats etc.

items.title: Pedestrian routing to subway station

labels.name: Routing

labels.name: Metro
labels.description: Subway, Tube, light-rail public transport issues

items.body:
**Describe the issue**
Pedestrian routing to the subway station should follow the same procedure as PT routing and guide to the closest subway entrance.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Plan a pedestrian routing to a subway station.
2. Compare to a PT routing including the same station as the beginning of the journey.

**Expected behavior**
The same as PT routing.

**System information:**
 - Organic Maps version: 2023.02.13-11-FDroid


Some subway stations are located underground. Routing to them doesn't make any sense. Another obvious improvement would be to hint to users visually or in some other way that the station is actually located underground, and they should look for an entrance. It can be done in different ways (changing icon, drawing entrances earlier - but without cluttering!, etc.)

items.title: Pedestrian Routing not preferring dedicated footways and crossings

labels.name: Routing
labels.description: Route building issues, e.g. valid route, valid ETA

items.body:
**Describe the issue**
For walk routing, OM is preferring to cross a `highway=primary` using a `highway=service` or `highway=residential` instead of the `highway=footway` + `footway=crossing`, even when length of route would be minimally impacted.


**Steps to reproduce**
1. Create a route which needs to cross a primary road that has pedestrian crossings and service roads, such as:
    - 40.664598, -111.938414 to 40.660618, -111.939485 (https://www.openstreetmap.org/directions?engine=fossgis_osrm_foot&route=40.664598%252C-111.938414%253B40.660618%252C-111.939485)
    - 40.674196, -111.938706 to 40.671629, -111.939086 (https://www.openstreetmap.org/directions?engine=fossgis_osrm_foot&route=40.674196%2C-111.938706%3B40.671629%2C-111.939086)
    - 40.653573, -111.957393 to 40.652660, -111.964702 (https://www.openstreetmap.org/directions?engine=fossgis_osrm_foot&route=40.653573%2C-111.957393%3B40.652660%2C-111.964702)


**Expected behaviour**
Pedestrian routing should give higher preference to using dedicated crossings, instead of where lower priority roads happen to intersect, especially given the examples of crossing a 7 lane primary road. On osm.org, OSRM foot routing is closest to desired behavior.


**System information:**
 - Operating system and its version: Android 14
 - Organic Maps version: 2024.11.27-12-Google
 - Device Model: Pixel 5

items.title: Routing for pedestrians should not avoid using primary roads.

labels.name: Routing
labels.description: Route building issues, e.g. valid route, valid ETA

items.body:
OM tries to avoid primary roads by default when routing for foot. Primary roads do not restrict the use by pedestrians unless specifically forbidden. Avoiding them by default results sometime in very awkward routings especially in an urban environment, because primary roads (usually national roads) mostly extend to the centre of cities. Therefore primary roads should always be allowed unless specifically tagged as foot=no. An option to avoid primary or busy roads would be preferred above the default as taken by OM.
The examples are from Halle Belgium Train station. 
![Schermafbeelding 2024-02-15 om 11 23 46](https://github.com/organicmaps/organicmaps/assets/157891098/fae33bcb-4fd3-4249-930e-b95966ae5c7e)
![Schermafbeelding 2024-02-15 om 11 23 00](https://github.com/organicmaps/organicmaps/assets/157891098/fd16d645-30d7-44d9-b9d1-afebd167c7e0)
The pictures show the straight path avoiding the use of the primary road and the path with an added stop follows as should be.

items.body:
After implementing street announcements in https://github.com/organicmaps/organicmaps/pull/3130 we got feedback from a user that streets are not announced when walking navigation is active. 

The assumption is that most sidewalks do not have names so they're not announced.

Sidewalks names are not rendered, because they pollute the map: https://github.com/organicmaps/organicmaps/pull/6789

Storing names of sidewalks from nearby streets just for announcements may influence the map data size and the search index. A better solution could be to query the nearby streets dynamically and get names to announce from them when building directions. @vng WDYT?

@zyphlar should #8412 be updated?

items.title: Walking mode route should ignore vehicle-only gates

labels.name: Routing
labels.description: Route building issues, e.g. valid route, valid ETA

items.body: **Describe the issue** On a hiking route that shares a segment with a road with restricted vehicle access, OM should respect the Allow Access tags from OSM that indicate roads/gates are open to pedestrians and/or cyclists (depending on routing mode). **Steps to reproduce** Route from end of NF Development Road 5510 where it meets Hansen Ridge Trail (47.359536, -121.539149) Route to Hansen Creek Trailhead (47.363961, -121.531193) Set mode to Walking **Expected behaviour** The router should use the shorter road segment. Adding an intermediate point on the road may force OM to use the segment, but this extra step shouldn't be necessary. **Screenshots** **System information:** - Operating system and its version: Android 17 - Organic Maps version: 2026.08.27-18-Google - Device Model: Google Pixel 7 **Additional context** The above example is part of an official hiking loop passes through a locked gate, and follows a short segment of road. Both the road and gate are marked as foot:yes, bicycles:yes in the Allow Access tags. Yet OM tries hard to avoid the road and route the long way around. After discussion via the Telegram group, we think it's the locked:yes tag on the gate itself that confuses the router. When the tags explicitly include foot:yes and bicycles:yes, the locked:yes tag should apply only to automobiles, and allow passage for pedestrians and cyclists. When the tags include foot:yes (but not bicycles:yes), the locked:yes tag should allow passage by pedestrians, but block automobiles and cyclists. When the tags include bicycles:yes (but not foot:yes), the locked:yes tag should allow passage by cyclists, but block automobiles and pedestrians. Barrier: https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/2428416980#map=20/47.3642863/-121.5318366&layers=VD with tags: ``` barrier=gate bicycle=yes foot=yes locked=yes material=metal ```

items.title: Render sidewalks mapped using `sidewalk=*` on a road
items.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
It's very useful for pedestrians to see whether a road has a sidewalk, but if the sidewalk is mapped in OSM using the `sidewalk=*` tag on a road instead of a separate way, it's not shown.


**Describe the ideal solution**
Imo ideal solution would be displaying additional way next to the road marked with `sidewalk=*`. This would be consistent with rendering sidewalks which are marked as separate ways in OSM


**Describe alternatives you have considered**
I actually don't know of any app that solves this problem - I tried OSMAnd, Mapy.cz... none of them show sidewalks mapped with the `sidewalk=*` tag either. OM could be the first one! :)


**Additional context**
#7952 may be required for implementing this.
